title: Swimming, diving, spearfishing and skin diving prohibited: John's Pass (north side)

title: Discharge of air, gas or spring-powered projectile weapons banned citywide, spearfishing excepted only where designated
effect: Firing any spring, gas or mechanically powered projectile weapon is unlawful anywhere in the city; the only spearfishing exception is 'in any area where such activity has been designated as permissible' by the city, state or federal government.
excerpt:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge any air gun or weapon from which a projectile is propelled by action of compressed air, the expansion of gas or a spring, or other mechanical means, or to discharge or shoot any cross bow, slingshot, bow and arrow or boomerang or to utilize any other similar weapon harmful or dangerous to wildlife or dangerous to human safety within the city except in defense of person or property.

(b) This section shall not be construed to prohibit the discharge of such weapons in the operation of properly licensed shooting galleries, on properties expressly approved for hunting by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or Division of Forestry, or to a person spear fishing in any area where such activity has been designated as permissible either by the city, the state or the federal government.
full: (c) excludes firearms (F.S. ch. 790). (d) penalty per § 1-15. History: (Ord. No. 16-22, § 1, 12-6-16).
scope: Entire City of Treasure Island.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. NEW. Conservative reading: a band or pneumatic speargun is a spring/gas/mechanical projectile weapon, so discharging one in city waters is unlawful unless the area is 'designated as permissible'. Whether general state-law legality counts as 'designated as permissible by the state' is ambiguous; the reading that closes more water is that no designation exists and the ban applies citywide, like St. Pete Beach § 54-4. title: Spear fishing prohibited within or near city waters
effect: Spearfishing of any kind (hand spear, sling, band or pneumatic gun) is unlawful within or near the territorial waters of the City of Venice.
excerpt:
(a) Definition. As used in this section, the term "spear fishing" means the taking or attempted taking of fish or other marine life from the territorial waters of the city by discharging, throwing, casting or hurling any spear, rod, arrow or other projectile for the purpose of spearing, piercing or impaling fish or other marine life, whether the projectile be propelled or manipulated by hand or by any airgun, spring gun or other contrivance, except that it shall not include the bringing of such game to gaff after being taken by ordinary methods of angling or netting, or the killing from the surface of dangerous marine life for the purpose of avoiding a public hazard, or the gigging of fish from the surface.

(b) Prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to engage or attempt to engage in spear fishing within or near the territorial waters of the city.
full: History note: (Code 1982, § 13-48). Chapter 46 art. IV div. 2 (Fishing and swimming). Division 3 (Skin and scuba diving) adds: § 46-132 diver's flag within 100 ft; § 46-134 no skin or scuba diving in any marked navigable channel unless authorized by the police department; § 46-135 no skin or scuba diving within 200 ft of any person fishing or any anchored boat. § 46-64: no diving from the Venice Fishing Pier or swimming within 150 ft of its centerline.
scope: 'Within or near the territorial waters of the city.' The city's territorial waters are not defined in the section. The Venice city limits include Gulf beaches from about Venice Inlet south past the Venice Fishing Pier and Caspersen Beach, and the Venice Inlet jetties. 'Near' has no stated distance.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. NEW and HIGH IMPACT. This is the only Gulf-coast city ordinance found that bans spearfishing outright across the whole city waterfront, including the Venice beach ledges and fossil-tooth dive sites. Conservative reading: treat all Gulf water off the Venice city limits out to the 9 nm state line as 'near', and the Venice Inlet and ICW within city limits as closed; at minimum draw the city limits extended seaward. Preemption: this regulates the taking of saltwater fish by name, the same § 379.2425 question as Treasure Island; untested, plan around it. Code current through Ord. No. 2026-19 (26 May 2026), Supp. No. 86 Update 1. title: City of Sarasota: spear fishing banned within 100 yards of city docks, bridges, piers, wharves and jetties at beaches and recreational areas; channel and flag rules
effect: Inside the City of Sarasota, no spearfishing within 100 yards of any city dock, bridge, pier, wharf or jetty at a recreational area or public bathing beach, and no skin diving, scuba or spearfishing in marked channels or within 200 ft of anglers or anchored boats.
excerpt:
Sec. 10-66. It shall be unlawful for any person to spear fish within a recreational area or public or municipal bathing beach within one hundred (100) yards of any dock, bridge, pier, wharf or jetty of the city.

Sec. 10-64. It shall be unlawful for any person to skin dive, scuba dive or spear fish within the bounds of any marked navigable channel unless permission is obtained from the appropriate law enforcement agency by the showing of some necessity for diving in such channel.

Sec. 10-65. It shall be unlawful for any person to skin dive, scuba dive or spear fish within two hundred (200) feet of any person fishing, or any boat anchored, prior to commencement of diving or spear fishing. There shall be excluded from the operation of this section any boat from which a diver is skin diving, scuba diving or spear fishing.
full: Sec. 10-62. It shall be unlawful for any person to skin dive, scuba dive or spear fish without displaying a diver's-down flag at a point not greater than one hundred (100) feet from the place of diving; provided that no flag shall be required of a person skin diving or scuba diving within two hundred (200) feet of the shoreline at a public recreational area or public or municipal bathing beach within the city. History notes: § 10-62 (Code 1971, § 11-17); § 10-64 (Code 1971, § 11-19); § 10-65 (Code 1971, § 11-20); § 10-66 (Code 1971, § 11-21). Ch. 10 art. III 'Skin and Scuba Diving and Spear Fishing'. § 10-4 separately bans diving from public bridges into the bays. §§ 10-61 and 10-63 not retrieved.
scope: City of Sarasota (separate from Sarasota County § 130-33). Lido Key, St. Armands, the city bayfront, Ringling Causeway and the New Pass / Big Pass areas inside city limits.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. NEW. This is the CITY of Sarasota; the existing sarasota-130-33 entry is the county. § 10-64 overlaps the county's channel rule. § 10-66 is a 100-YARD buffer around city-owned structures only where they sit in a recreational area or public bathing beach. Conservative reading: draw 100 yd around every city pier, jetty and bridge touching a public beach or park (Lido Beach, North Lido, South Lido, Ringling Causeway parks). Code current through Ord. No. 26-5592 (20 Apr 2026), Supp. 33 Update 1. title: Spearfishing gear banned on the beach and in the water; scuba confined to a designated area; 100-yard pier zone
effect: At Dania Beach, spearguns, slings, gigs, bows and pole spears are banned on the beach and in the water; snorkelers may go no further than 50 yards out except from the designated diving area at the south end of Ocean Park; nobody may swim, scuba or skin dive within 100 yards of the Ocean Park fishing pier.
excerpt:
(b) It shall be unlawful to fish from a boat, to fish from the beach, to fish from the surf, to swim, to scuba dive, to skin-dive or bring or allow any boat to come within an area of one hundred (100) yards from the outside perimeter of the municipally-owned fishing pier at Ocean Park beach. ...

(c) Snorkeling will be permitted up to a limit of fifty (50) yards into the Atlantic Ocean, measured eastward from the high tide line of all public beach areas, except as stated above. Snorkeling beyond fifty (50) yards off the public beach is prohibited unless a person is entering the water in the designated diving area at the southernmost end of the public beach or express permission is given by a lifeguard or the supervising lifeguard. Artificial breathing devices, such as scuba-tanks, aqua-lungs or hooka rigs, when used in the waters of the area known as, Ocean Park are confined to the designated diving area at the southernmost end of Ocean Park, unless express permission to use such devices elsewhere along the beach is obtained from a lifeguard or the supervising lifeguard. The use of spearfishing guns, gigs, slings, bows, and, pole spears on the beach, in the water, or both is prohibited.
full: (b) continues: no boats in marked restricted areas within 100 yds offshore; no fishing or surf casting from the public beach 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; no fishing from any boat within 300 yds of the low water mark along the entire Atlantic beach in the city; balloon fishing prohibited. full: History: § 5-4 (Code 1962, § 5-4.1); § 5-5 (Code 1962, § 5-4(b); Ord. No. 2009-27, § 1, 10-13-2009); § 5-7 (Code 1962, § 5-1; Ord.
